title: terraform(private): consolidate GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and state layout for Private deployments
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need a consistent Terraform surface for GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking resources (VPC/subnets/peering), and a clearer remote state layout to support upgrades and multi-environment installs. This PR consolidates multiple ad-hoc modules we had across redwood-private into a single opinionated set of modules with stable inputs and outputs so Dedicated/Private installers and the installer operator can rely on the same state layout.

What this changes:
- Introduces modules/priv_gpu_node_pool: parameterized GPU node pools with GPU type/accelerator profiles, taints/labels, machine images, and autoscaling policies.
- Introduces modules/priv_iam: consolidated IAM roles/policies for node bootstrap, image pull, kms access, and control-plane networking. Minimal privileges principle applied and roles are separated per component (installer, runtime, monitoring).
- Introduces modules/priv_networking: VPC/subnet/route table/peering module tailored for Private installs with optional shared VPC and a 'bastion' public subnet toggle.
- Changes remote state layout: splits state into logical buckets: networking.tfstate, nodepools.tfstate, iam.tfstate, installer.tfstate to allow safer incremental applies and targeted rollbacks.
- Migration helpers: small helper script (scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh) and documentation in modules/README.md describing the state split and recommended migration steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Module implementation with acceptance tests (unit-level terraform validate + plan)
- [x] Backwards-compatible inputs where possible and migration steps documented
- [x] CI passes terraform fmt/checks and kcd (kept consistent with other infra repos)
- [x] Reviews from infra and security teams

Notes on compatibility: Default behavior preserves previous names and tags when no explicit new inputs are provided. Where name changes were unavoidable for state splitting we provide explicit migration commands and a one-time mapping script included in scripts/. The state split is opt-in by setting terraform_remote_state.layout = "split" for now; we will flip the default after we complete one customer migration.

Related: ENG-4821 (private installer state and upgrade reliability), ENG-4870 (gpu autoscaling profiles), SUP-1598 (customer reported installer failure during upgrade). Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/private-deployment-state-layout (internal).
commit_summary: feat(module): add modules/priv_gpu_node_pool with GPU profiles and autoscaling
feat(module): add modules/priv_iam and least-privilege role separation
feat(module): add modules/priv_networking with optional shared VPC and bastion
chore(tfstate): implement split remote state layout and migration helpers
test: add terratest/validate scripts for new modules
review_conversation: Diego Ramos: Left high-level feedback on IAM scope - requested removing wildcard on kms:Decrypt in node role. Asked for clearer separation between installer and runtime roles.
Asha Patel: Addressed by breaking kms permissions into a dedicated role for image-decryption and limited to resource ARNs. Added documentation explaining role boundaries.
Maya Chen: Noted that node taints need a default for older installs; requested a default taint map to preserve backwards compatibility.
Asha Patel: Added default taints and an explicit 'preserve_existing_taints' flag for upgrades. Added unit test to cover missing taint input.

Ben Carter: Ran terraform plan against staging and reported a small drift due to subnet name normalization. Suggested name suffix normalization function - added helper in modules/priv_networking/names.tf.
Security (review): Approved after seeing least-privilege IAM adjustments and audit logging for role changes. Asked that migration steps be run during maintenance windows - added note in README.
CI: initial run failed on fmt/lint; fixes were pushed and CI passed on re-run. Acceptance tests (validate) passed in CI environment.
Maya Chen: Approved the PR with one follow-up issue to monitor nodepool autoscale behavior under heavy startup load (ENG-4902).
Mergebot: Merged via squash after approvals and green CI.
release_notes: Adds new Terraform modules for private deployments: priv_gpu_node_pool, priv_iam, priv_networking. Introduces an opt-in split remote state layout and migration helpers. Enables safer, targeted applies and rollbacks for Private installs. See modules/README.md for migration steps.
notes: This PR is part of a larger effort to harden Private installer upgrades. Operators should follow the migration instructions in modules/README.md and test in staging before enabling the split remote state layout in production.
